mainEntity.name: Should I build an attached in-law suite or a detached mother-in-law apartment?

acceptedAnswer.text: The decision between an attached suite and a detached unit comes down to yard space, budget, and desired privacy. An attached addition builds directly onto your existing home, making it easier and often less expensive to connect to current plumbing, electrical, and HVAC systems. It also keeps aging parents closer under one roofline. A detached accessory dwelling unit offers maximum independence and acoustic separation for both households, but it requires sufficient lot square footage and independent utility trenching. Your property setbacks and zoning rules will help dictate which approach fits your land.
acceptedAnswer.description: Attached suites connect directly to the main house and share utilities more easily, while detached units provide greater acoustic privacy and independence but require more yard space.
